# BOOK 1 (The Fatal Three, Vol. I–III, Braddon) — NOTES

Source: Gutenberg 75410–75412. Three volumes merged. Vol I = Book the First "Clotho; or Spinning the Thread" (ch I–XIV). Vol II = Book the Second "Lachesis; or the Meter of Destiny" (ch I–IX). Vol III = Book the Third "Atropos; or That Which Must Be" (ch I–XI). Title page: "The Fatal Three, by the author of Lady Audley's Secret, Vixen, Ishmael, Mohawks." Publisher Simpkin, Marshall & Co.

## Vol I

**Ch I "We have been so happy."** Mrs Maud Fausset (née Hon. Maud Donfrey, third dau. of Lord Castle-Connell, Irish peer; 19 at marriage; 9 years married) and husband John Fausset (stout, middle-aged, wholesale silk fortune from firm near St Paul's Churchyard, Lyons factory; now out of trade) live in Upper Parchment Street, off Grosvenor Square. Daughter Mildred (7, golden hair, doll). John asks Maud to adopt orphan Fay (13–14), his ward, distant relation, heiress, sole trustee Maud's... actually John is sole trustee. Maud objects ("a horrid rebellious girl"). Mildred begs "Let the little girl come." Maud consents. Mildred's favourite doll: walking-talking one from Paris.

**Ch II "Fay."** Fay arrives in hansom with John; tall, thin, pale, black eyes, olive complexion, badly dressed, "a look of never having been much cared for." Maud calls her an owl-eyed plain girl. Fay: "I love books," "I hate lessons." Fay gives Mildred affection. Fay is given Bell's room (servant's room, back, mews view). Bell is nurse/servant; John objects. Fay's room is dismal. Maud fears Fay will not marry. The Hook = Fausset's riverside villa, Chertsey–Windsor. Streatham Common is where Fay came from.

**Ch III "A Superior Person."** Mildred and Fay bond. Bell (Martha Bell, 48, ex-wet nurse at Castle-Connell, ex-wife of gardener Patrick Bell, emigrated to Canada, died) hates Fay, dominates household. Bell says Fay is "his natural daughter" (rumour). Maud says Fay is "sly." Fay refuses Bell's help. Miss Colville = morning governess. Bell remarks Fay "dropped from the moon."

**Ch IV "All She Could Remember."** Fay's past: childhood in cottage on windy chalky hill above sea (France, "Nounou", cow, hens, tall column with statue); "Where do they go?" was first remembered speech. Sent to school (Miss Constable's, Brussels-like seminary; expelled after temper outburst in class). Summer at The Hook: Mildred ill with scarlet fever (scarlatina); Fay nurses her. Meta = German maid. Bell and Meta gossip overheard by Mildred: Fay "is his daughter"/sister. Mildred asks Maud to let her call Fay "sister"; Maud furious; Fay says "I hate everybody else in this house"; Maud: "You are a wicked, ungrateful girl." John: "She was once near and dear to me." Fay sent to Brussels finishing-school; Mildred told in letter (Bell reads it). Fay gone; Mildred weeps.

**Ch V "Without the Wolf."** Years later (Mildred Greswold's era). George Greswold, Enderby Manor (near Romsey, Hampshire; Test valley; Enderby Manor built under William III). Daughter Lola (12, golden hair, blue eyes). Greswold wife Mildred (formerly Fausset). Lola: "Red Riding Hood, only without the wolf." Village fever (typhoid) — eleven cases. Dr Porter (village doctor, "Mr. Porter"). Polly Rainbow (flaxen-haired, carries milk pitcher from dairy). Joe Stanning, Johnny Giles, Mary Martin, Janet Dawson, Andrew Rogers, Mrs Peter. Mrs Wadman (dairywoman, bailiff Thomas, husband Wadman). Source: old well near manure heap in dairy garden, used for dairy washing. Greswold's model estate, Dr Hutchinson (Southampton). Lola's study pavilion; Latin with Horace; Bell (white-haired, 74, nursed Lola's grandmother).

**Ch VI "Ah! Pity! The Lily is Withered."** Lola ill; Polly Rainbow dies; Lola dies (~ten days after; funeral bell). Greswold plans Scotland. Widow Rainbow: "She was all I had." Greswold: "My God... three or four people murdered." Lola's last words: "Father said she was better."

**Ch VII "Drifting Apart."** Greswolds at Villa on Lake of Thun, Switzerland. Greswold's "bad dream": "The cage—the cage again—iron bars—like a wild beast!" Mildred's reflections on Fay. Mildred's memories: Fay's mother = Mrs Fausset (Maud) died; Maud on death-bed told Mildred Fay was John's natural daughter by a woman before John's marriage, "I hated her". Mildred now ~31. Maud died soon after Mildred's 16th birthday. Mildred under Bell's watch. Heart of Midlothian reference.

**Ch VIII "Such Things Were."** Greswold's meeting with Mildred at The Hook (summer, she 17, he 13 years older). He had been introduced by John Fausset (old Oxford friend; Greswold's father George Ransome of Magdalen). Greswold = born George Ransome; mother left him Enderby; brother Randolph; father Squire Ransome of Mapledown (Sussex). Assumed name Greswold. Vienna winter. Back to Enderby: dismissal of servants (Wadman, Thomas, etc.). Mildred at Lola's grave (Lola's epitaph: "Laura, the only child of George and Mildred Greswold, aged twelve"). Greswold at grave cries "Judgment! judgment!"

**Ch IX "The Face in the Church."** Mildred & Greswold conversation about Pamela Ransome (Randolph's daughter, 2 sisters; sister Rosalind married Sir Henry Mountford of Rainham Hall). Pamela invited to Manor. Kassandra = Irish setter. Mildred sees Judas-faced stranger with auburn beard in Enderby church (Te Deum).

**Ch X "There is always the skeleton."** Riverdale = Hillersdon house; Tom Hillersdon, millionaire; wife Louise Hillersdon (formerly Louise Lorraine, adventuress). Stranger = César Castellani (Milanese; father composer; author of "Nepenthe"). He tells Mildred that her father Fausset had silk business ties with Felix & Sons of Lyons; he saw her as golden child in Hyde Park. He reveals Greswold's first marriage at Nice (Lady Lochinvar's palace). Greswold pale.

**Ch XI "Beginning of Doubt."** Greswold says first wife unknown; Mildred suspicious. Pamela arrives (fox-terrier Box, son of Brockenhurst Joe). Pamela "Agnostic"; admires Castellani.

**Ch XII "She cannot be unworthy."** Castellani calls again; mention of Clement Cancellor (Vicar of St Elizabeth's, Parchment Street; Mildred's childhood tutor). Mildred agrees Mrs Hillersdon may come.

**Ch XIII "Shall she be less than another?"** Cancellor's history with Louise. Dinner: Deceased Wife's Sister Bill debate; Greswold vs Cancellor; Rollinson (curate, Enderby, Mr. Frederick Rollinson). Castellani sings Heine/Jensen; Mildred weeps. Concert arranged (for Burne-Jones window, Enderby).

**Ch XIV "Lifting the Curtain."** Castellani pushes concert. Mildred demands truth from Greswold in library. Greswold shows portrait of first wife: "small, delicate face, large dark eyes." Mildred faints. END VOL I.

## Vol II

**Ch I "A Wife and No Wife."** Castellani background (Magnus Dudley, society poet; Coutts's account). Louise & Castellani talk at Riverdale. Concert day: Castellani dresses rooms. Pamela sings duet "'Twere sweet to die as the roses die." Mildred ill. Mildred flees by carriage to Ivy Cottage (Miss Fisher's), then Waterloo. Letter from Mildred to Greswold: she believes his first marriage was to her half-sister (Fay), so their marriage unlawful. Mildred writes to Pamela too.

**Ch II "The Sins of the Fathers."** Greswold interrogates Bell: Bell says Fay was John's daughter. Fay's mother/first wife = Vivien Faux (name Greswold married in Florence, British consul, 19 years ago, aged ~18-ish; trustee lawyer in Lincoln's Inn).

**Ch III "The Verdict of Her Church."** Mildred travels to London; stays at Queen Anne's Gate with Mrs Cecilia Tomkison (husband Adam Tomkison, Mexican Street Railways) and lives near Queen Anne's Mansions (Castellani's rooms). Mildred consults Clement Cancellor (rusty black coat), who says marriage invalid in conscience. Greswold letter: he defends marriage; wife's sister argument. Mildred replies: Fay was her half-sister (mother's death-bed confession).

**Ch IV "No Light."** Miss Gertrude Fausset (John's sister, 57, Lewes Crescent, Brighton; silver-gray rooms; Franz the Swiss butler; Louisa Mildred's maid). Mildred tells her story; Gertrude denies knowledge, advises return to husband. Castellani arrives at Lewes Crescent, plays Bach; plays opera "La Donna del Pittore" (his father's). Gertrude's brother John Fausset.

**Ch V "The Future Might Be Darker."** Greswold's history: Vivien Faux (orphan, life interest £30,000 Consols via Pergament & Pergament, Lincoln's Inn Fields). Greswold meets Mr Pergament (solicitor), refused info. Takes Pamela to Brighton. Greswold tells Mildred "the future might be still darker." Pamela, Box, Brighton. Rev. Maltravers (Vicar of St Edmund's, Brighton, heavy brows, wants transept) and curate Percival Cromer.

**Ch VI "Higher Views."** Mildred ill (low fever). Pallanza plan. Pamela and Castellani. Maltravers pleads Mildred stay in Brighton. Gertrude & Castellani: Castellani's father's history; Gertrude's secret ("I loved him").

**Ch VII "The Time Has Come."** Mildred, Pamela travel to Pallanza (Lago Maggiore), then Castellani pursues Pamela. Castellani confesses love for Mildred; Mildred rejects him, threatens. Castellani: "a madman and a murderer." Mildred to Genoa and Nice.

**Ch VIII "Not Proven."** Castellani's accusation: Ransome (Greswold) was suspected of killing wife (at St Jean, near Nice) and confined in Nice asylum. Mildred at Nice: Lady Lochinvar (Palais Montano, Nice; nephew Malcolm Stuart; former Irish O'Labacolly daughter). Lady Lochinvar tells: Vivien Faux (Mrs Ransome) threw herself or was pushed off cliff near Villefranche/St Jean; Ransome arrested, confined at asylum on road to St André; "not proven."

**Ch IX "Looking Back."** Mildred visits Villa Le Bout du Monde (now Montfleuri) at St Jean; caretaker market-woman; cook's cousin. Madhouse at St André: Monsieur Leroy (doctor, 60). Maria Castellani (Paolo's cousin, singer, mad). Mildred visits Ransome's room. Pamela & Mr Stuart. END VOL II.

## Vol III

**Ch I "A Wrecked Life."** Mildred visits asylum singer Maria Castellani; learns Paolo Castellani's history (married French consumptive). Mildred plans to fund piano for Maria.

**Ch II "In the Morning of Life."** Greswold's solitude at Enderby; reads Pamela's letters. Greswold's youth: father Squire Ransome of Mapledown; brother Randolph; mother; Schliemann; Florence. Meets Vivien Faux at Signora Vicenti's party (black velvet). Mortimer (English artist, guardian); marriage after Greswold's pity.

**Ch III "The Rift in the Lute."** St Jean villa (life; Vivien jealous). Delia Darcy & sister (Irish girls). Quarrel on cliff path; Vivien flings herself off; Ransome left alone.

**Ch IV "Darkness."** Vivien dead on rocks; fishermen. Inquest at Villefranche, Juge d'Instruction. Ransome imprisoned, then mad (grandiose Italian Republic delusion); asylum. Released; mother's death 1869 gave him money.

**Ch V "The Grave on the Hill."** Mildred visits Enderby churchyard? No — Mildred at St Jean graveyard; Fay's grave ("VIVIEN RANSOME. Died April 24th, 1868"); Mildred plants roses. Malcolm Stuart introduced to Pamela.

**Ch VI "Pamela Changes Her Mind."** Castellani pursues Pamela again at Nice; Pamela cools toward him, falls for Malcolm Stuart. Mrs Montagu W. Brown. Miss Fausset dies later. Mildred called to Brighton by Maltravers.

**Ch VII "As the Sands Run Down."** Mildred at Lewes Crescent. Gertrude weak. Mildred writes to Rollinson; Rollinson's reply: Greswold's heart broken, visits Lola's grave at dusk. Mildred returns to Enderby churchyard; "George! George!"

**Ch VIII "How Should I Greet Thee?"** Mildred and Greswold at grave; coolness. Mildred visits Rollinson at carpenter's lodging (Mrs Mason). Brighton. Mildred & Gertrude; Pamela engaged to Malcolm Stuart; honeymoon at The Hook.

**Ch IX "Litera Scripta Manet."** Mildred at The Hook finds letters in cupboard (Fay's letters from Milan, Mrs Holmby chaperon; Castellani; Evian; Fanny/Fay born 1868?; deed of gift £30,000 India Stock to Fanny Fausset alias Vivien Faux). Letters written by Gertrude to brother John reveal Fay was Gertrude's (?) — actually Fay's letters from Gertrude; the infant was Gertrude's daughter by Paolo Castellani. Mildred rushes home.

**Ch X "Marked by Fate."** Mildred returns to Enderby; reconciled with Greswold. Heart trouble; Dr Porter; London physician. Mildred's health declines.

**Ch XI "Like a Tale that is Told."** Pamela's wedding in Westminster Abbey. Gertrude's confession (Castellani's father Paolo; Gertrude married him in sham civil marriage, fooled; child = Fay). Gertrude dies early winter; Mildred inherits. Greswold Hospital founded; Greswolds' line ends. Castellani later faded.

END OF BOOK 1.

BOOK 2 (When Freemen Shall Stand, Nelson S. Bond, Fantastic Adventures Nov 1943) — NOTES

**Ch I.** Stephen "Steve" Duane (chemist, army lieutenant) and Chuck Lafferty (sergeant, lab assistant) at Fort Knox-like lab, WWII. Spy Eric von Rath (German, guard disguise, Nazi). Duane tests anaesthetic gas "methioprane". Von Rath drops/breaks flask; all three frozen into statues in a glass tomb inside Fort Knox ("Fautnox"). Awaken in 3500s.

**Ch II.** Priestess Beth (dust-gold hair, golden breast-cups). Mother Maatha of Tucki Clan. Warrior captain Jain. Breeders, workers, warriors (Women). Venus = "Daan" planet. Wild Ones (males). Chanted US anthem mangled. Duane identified as "Dwain".

**Ch III.** Mother explains Daan (Venusian) invasion ~100 seasons ago. Methioprane needs swamp-musk seeds. Von Rath made truce. Mother's records: "Place of the Gods" = Mt Rushmore in 'Kota (South Dakota). Beth chooses Steve as mate. Reds = Cincinnati (Netherland Plaza) = Sinnaty.

**Ch IV.** Battle with Wild Ones (leader Jon). Duane tricks Women into letting Wild Ones in as men; priestess Beth draws a golden knife. Revelation: Gods were Men.

**Ch V.** Journey to Sinnaty (Cincinnati). Glass bridge (Venusian plastic). Captured by Daans, Sinnaty tower = Nedlunplaza (Netherland Plaza). Overlord Loala (silver hair, gray-green eyes).

**Ch VI–VII.** Prison tower. Rodrik of Mish-kin (traitor, Brotherhood member, blond Venusian-looking). Duane defeats Rodrik in fist-fight (Queensbury rules). Jak of Norlinz (new lieutenant). Duane becomes "ruler" of prisoners.

**Ch VIII–IX.** Overlord Loala: "The Brotherhood" (human collaborators). Loala's "Treatment" (brain-imprint cylinder; destruction = death). Steve given Daan brain-image; sent to Fautnox to hunt Slumberers.

**Ch X–XI.** Rodrik defects, pursues to Sinnaty; Duane captured again; Overlord Okuno (secretly human, Wiam of Kleevlun) swapped cylinders; Rodrik "executed." Earth uprising begins; Okuno as rebel masquerader.

**Ch XII–XIII.** Steve given disguise as "Captain Huumo," flies on spaceship Oalumuo with Loala. Ten-day trip to Daan (Venus).

**Ch XIV–XV.** Daan palace; Supreme Council (three decadent Masters); slave camp in equatorial marshes; Amarro (guard, secret human ally). Chuck and Beth in camp. Von Rath survives (amnesia cured).

**Ch XVI–XVII.** Chuck: swamp-musk = klaar = methioprane ingredient. Amarro's underground refuge on island; ultra-wave link with Okuno. Rebellion begins on Earth.

**Ch XVIII–XX.** Steve captured (Loala's ruse with Beth's voice). Loala offers brain-operation to save him; bargain (amnesty for rebels). Von Rath attacks; killed by Steve. Loala burnt by von Rath's ray, put in suspended sleep by methioprane. Humans seize Daan armada via methioprane in air ducts. Armada split; Earth gets half. Steve, Chuck, Beth, Mother Maatha return to Earth. Closing: Beth: "a man"; Star-Spangled Banner verse; "And thus be it ever when freemen shall stand..."; "For a woman always has the last word."
